author: mindmap-write-lane-c
readerQuestion: How much will a hard money loan cost me in total? [PAA 2/6 on-topic (how do hard money loans work; how do you calculate loan to cost), 4/6 off-topic: personal loan monthly cost, mortgage affordability; ac 3/16 question completions incl. how much hard money loan cost, is hard money loan interest only]

presentation.placement: New real-estate spoke; calculator is section 1
presentation.reason: Cost depends on loan size, rate, points, months held and optional after-repair value, so the reader must enter their deal.
readerInputs: Percent of purchase price the lender advances
Selling costs percent and monthly holding costs (optional)

interaction.reason: Each input changes total financing cost, loan-to-cost and profit; a static example cannot answer a reader whose points or hold time differ.

animation.reason: A month-by-month interest table is clearer than motion; reduced-motion safe by default.

caseDecisions: Retrieved with the exact approved reader question. 8 candidates, none about 401(k) plan loans, short-term real estate loans or ModernWallet readers: they are other Layer3Labs properties, client engagements and a gaming testimonial. ModernWallet's _experience.md has no named-client specifics. Rejected all; no client claim on the page.
exclusions: No TESTED label and no reviewed-by claim: financial service, _experience.md section G excludes it and no product test exists. Internal-modeling wording only.
decisionGap: Readers find calculators that return a payment, but the total cost of a short interest-only loan is points plus months of interest plus fees plus any extension, and the months held move it more than the rate does. Sampled the 2026-11-14 research pack and DataForSEO read; no site-wide uniqueness claimed.
finding: In our internal modeling of one example deal (purchase $200,000, rehab $50,000, lender advances 90% of the purchase and 100% of the rehab, 12% APR, 2 points, 6 months, $2,500 in other fees), the loan is $230,000, points are $4,600, interest-only payments are $2,300 a month, interest over 6 months is $13,800, total financing cost is $20,900, the balloon payoff is $230,000 and loan to cost is 92%. Changing months by 3 moves the total by $6,900; one point or 2 points of APR moves it by $2,300. A 3-month extension with a 1% fee adds $9,200 ($6,900 interest and a $2,300 fee). With an example after-repair value of $330,000, 6% selling costs and $1,000 a month of holding costs, loan to ARV is 69.7% and profit before tax is $33,300.
conditions: Reader-entered terms only; every rate, point and fee in the example is an illustrative input, not a lender quote or market figure. Interest is simple and interest-only on the full balance (rehab funded at closing); a drawn-evenly option lowers interest on the example to $12,550. Profit is before tax. Default interest, draw inspection fees and prepayment minimums are not modelled unless entered as fees.
whatWouldChange: A lender quote with different points, rate, fees or hold time; a different draw schedule; a loan that is not interest-only; extension or default terms; taxes on the profit.
method: Deterministic: loan = purchase x advance% + rehab x advance%; points = loan x points%; interest = sum of monthly balance x APR/12; total financing cost = points + fees + interest + extension interest + extension fee; LTC = loan/(purchase + rehab); LTARV = loan/ARV; profit = ARV - selling costs - purchase - rehab - financing cost - holding costs. Python replica of src/lib/hard-money-loan.ts.
limitations: No market rates or lender terms; simple annualized cost is total cost over the loan and years held, not an IRR; pre-tax; no default interest or prepayment minimums; no judgment on whether a deal is good.
counterexample: At 0% APR the total falls to $7,100 (points and fees only), so points and fees alone do not explain a 6-month total of $20,900; and drawing the rehab evenly instead of at closing cuts interest from $13,800 to $12,550, so the same terms cost less when money is drawn later.
